title: Asking the way
goal: Asking for directions, understanding the answer, and getting around by public transport — a unit that brings back the prepositions of unit 6, the commands of unit 16, and the numbers of unit 7 in one real task.
bekal: ask for directions and understand the answer
name means of transport and haggle over the fare
talk about distance and travel time

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د کوڅې پر سر
dialogs.intro: Budi is lost among the lanes of the old bazaar. The map on his phone is no help, but a bread seller has more time than any map.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Excuse me, can I ask you something?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه د پښتنو باغ لټوم. چېرته دی؟
lines.baca: zə də paṣtano bāgh laṭawəm. cherta day?
lines.id: I'm looking for Pashtunistan Park. Where is it?
lines.literal: I of Pashtun garden look-for-I. where is?

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: لرې نه دی. مخ ته ولاړ شه، بیا ښي لور ته.
lines.baca: lare nə day. makh ta wlāṛ sha, byā ṣəy lor ta.
lines.id: It's not far. Go straight, then turn right.
lines.literal: far not is. front to going become, then right direction to.

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: شاوخوا درې سوه متره. د جومات تر څنګه تېر شه.
lines.baca: shāwkhwā dre swa metra. də jumāt tər tsanga ter sha.
lines.id: About three hundred meters. Go past the mosque.
lines.literal: about three hundred meters. of mosque from side past become.

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: یو لوی څلورلاری. هلته کیڼ لور ته وګرځه.
lines.baca: yaw loy tsalorlārī. halta kīṇ lor ta wə́gardza.
lines.id: A big crossroads. Turn left there.
lines.literal: one big crossroads. there left direction to turning become.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: And will I see the park?

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: هو، سمدلاسه. لویه دروازه یې شنه ده.
lines.baca: ho, samdlāsa. lawya darwāza ye shna da.
lines.id: Yes, right away. Its big gate is green.
lines.literal: yes, at-once. big gate of-it green is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: How long does it take on foot?

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: لس دقیقې، نه ډېر. که ستړی یې، رکشه ونیسه.
lines.baca: las daqīqe, nə ḍer. ka stəṛay ye, riksha wə́nīsa.
lines.id: Ten minutes, no more. If you're tired, take a rickshaw.
lines.literal: ten minutes, not much. if tired are-you, rickshaw take.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: How much does a rickshaw charge?

lines.speaker: ناناوی:
lines.text: پنځوس افغانۍ. خو مخکې بیه وټاکه!
lines.baca: pindzos afghānəy. kho məkhke bīya wə́ṭāka!
lines.id: Fifty afghani. But agree on the price first!
lines.literal: fifty afghani. but before price set!

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Thanks a lot. May you not get tired!

notes: The greeting ورورجانه means "dear brother", and Afghans use it with strangers of about their own age. Other forms you'll hear: **لالا** *lālā* (older brother, to someone older), **کاکا** *kākā* (uncle, to a much older man), **خورجانې** to a woman.
Directions in Pashto use the command form for ته, even with strangers. مخ ته ولاړ شه isn't rude; it's the usual way to give directions, and even a friendly bread seller will use it.

The word لور means "direction" and always pairs with the postposition ته — for example ښي **لور ته** for to the right · کیڼ **لور ته** for to the left. Note that this لور is not the same word as لور meaning daughter; the two just happen to be spelled alike.
The phrase تر څنګه تېر شه means "go past it". The verb تېرېدل (to pass) turns up in lots of directions, and it pairs with تر ... څنګه like the pairs in unit 6.

⚠️ The advice مخکې بیه وټاکه (agree on the price first) applies to taxis, rickshaws, and anything without a meter. Asking the price after you arrive is the quickest way to pay double, and that's true everywhere, not just in Afghanistan.

Distance is often given as travel time, not meters. The answers you'll hear most are لس دقیقې (ten minutes) or نږدې دی (it's close), and figures in meters are actually rare. If you need precision, ask twice in different ways.

grammars.title: Asking the way, and understanding the answer
body: The three questions in the first rows of the table cover almost every need. The harder part is understanding the answer, which is why rows four to eight are worth memorizing as whole sounds.
If you don't catch the answer, don't just nod. Say **بخښنه، بیا ووایه** or point with your hand and ask **دې لور ته؟** — people will happily correct you.

grammars.title: Distance and travel time
body: Pashto gives distance with the verb **وخت نیسي** (it takes time) or simply with how long it lasts. For the way you travel, it uses the pair **په ... کې** for a closed vehicle and **په پښو** for on foot.
Note the form په پښو: the word پښه (foot) stands in the oblique plural پښو. This is the form you set up in unit 6, and here it works without any postposition.

blocks.text: Places you need to be able to ask for

blocks.title: Four phrases that keep you from ever being truly lost
items: To open: **بخښنه غواړم، یوه پوښتنه لرم** — "excuse me, can I ask you something?". This phrase opens doors anywhere.
To check: **دې لور ته؟** *de lor ta* — "this way?", pointing with your whole hand, not one finger.
To ask for a repeat: **بخښنه، بیا ووایه** — "sorry, please say it again". Add **ورو** if you need it slower.
To give up politely: **زه دلته نوی یم** *zə dəlta naway yəm* — "I'm new here". This almost always brings more patient help, and sometimes someone to walk you all the way there.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Pointing, and the small things that matter
items: Point the way with your **whole open hand**, not your index finger. Pointing at people with a finger is considered rude in most of Afghanistan.
If you're a woman asking a man you don't know, a calm distance and tone matter more than the words. Asking another woman or a stallholder is the most comfortable choice.
Afghans rarely say "I don't know" to a question about directions, because it feels like refusing to help. If the answer sounds unsure, ask a second person before walking far.
Street addresses are hardly used. Landmarks are: **د جومات تر څنګه** (beside the mosque), **د بانک مخې ته** (in front of the bank). Learn to name landmarks, not house numbers.
Excuse me, can I ask you something?
How do I get to the airport?

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: بخښنه غواړم، یوه پوښتنه لرم. — باغ چېرته دی؟ — هوایي ډګر ته څنګه ولاړ شم؟ — څومره لرې دی؟ — زه دلته نوی یم.
ولاړ شه — وګرځه — وګرځه — تېر شه — وګرځه
باغ چېرته دی؟ — مخ ته ولاړ شه. — ښي لور ته وګرځه. — څومره وخت نیسي؟ — زه دلته نوی یم.
wave: Picture the route from your home to work or school, then say the directions in Pashto as if to a stranger. Four sentences are enough, and if you get stuck at a turn, that's the word to add tomorrow.
